# Four catches decide "departed window" with three different predicates

## Context

#19061 (#19056) settles an **unhandled** `NEO_DEAD_PORT` rejection only when the window it targeted departed: `reason.code === 'NEO_DEAD_PORT' && isWindowDeparted(reason.windowId ?? reason.destination)`. That is the two-half predicate #18741 established. Four call sites catch the same rejection themselves, because each also has a second purpose: naming its subsystem, or settling `Neo.isDestroyed`. They decide "departed" in two different ways:

| site | predicate |
|---|---|
| `container/Viewport.mjs:144` | both halves (`NEO_DEAD_PORT` + `isWindowDeparted(windowId)`) |
| `draggable/DragZone.mjs:445` | code only |
| `grid/Body.mjs:1321` | code only (+ `Neo.isDestroyed`) |
| `table/Body.mjs:631` | code only (+ `Neo.isDestroyed`) |

## The Problem

The code-only sites swallow a dead port whose window **never existed**, which is a real misroute. #19067 is the latest proof that one exists: a message for a departed window was being delivered to a sibling. The central boundary would surface that error; these four sites silence it. It is the same rule written four times with two meanings. @neo-opus-ada agreed to the shared predicate on #19061's fork.

## The Fix

Add one predicate, `worker.Base#isDeparture(reason, windowId)`, that answers the two halves. `onUnhandledRejection` and the four catches call it in place of their inline tests. The code-only sites tighten to both halves; their `Neo.isDestroyed` handling and subsystem messages stay as they are.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1** — `isDeparture` exists on `worker.Base`, and `onUnhandledRejection` uses it with no change in behaviour (the existing `WindowDeparture` arms stay green).
- [ ] **AC-2** — Each of the four sites uses it. A departed window stays silent there, and a never-known dead port now reaches its subsystem's `console.error`. One unit arm per site covers the newly visible case.
- [ ] **AC-3** — No inline `NEO_DEAD_PORT` comparison remains in `src` outside `worker/Base.mjs`.

## Out of Scope

- Deleting any of the four catches. Each has a named second purpose (#19061's AC-4).
- The `DomEvent` and `Overflow` sites, which check before the call and skip the work.

## Related

- #19056 / #19061 — central settlement
- #18741 — the departure predicate
- #19067 — the misroute a code-only predicate hides
- #19011 — Viewport's both-halves precedent
